# PARK LEAVES — publisher and content records

## Publication
- Publisher and book title: PARK LEAVES.
- Subtitle: Six trees for British parks.
- Audience: urban nature observers.
- Edition: First edition, 2026.
- Publication imprint: PARK LEAVES.
- Handbook design credit: Handbook design: PARK LEAVES.
- Copyright line for new handbook text and layout: Copyright 2026 PARK LEAVES.
- Historical illustration credit category: Historical botanical illustrations.
- Print quantity: 300 copies.
- Page count: 12, including front and back covers.
- Nominal closed trim: 105 × 148 mm.
- Exterior trim: 210 × 148 mm.
- Bleed: 3 mm on exterior edges.
- Paper: 140 gsm uncoated throughout.
- Printing: four-colour digital.
- Binding: saddle stitched.
- Allocated spine panel: 0 mm; folded edge.
- Exterior text locations: front and back panels.
- Page grid: two columns; 8 mm margins on all four sides; 4 mm gutter; column width 42.5 mm.
- Body type category: serif; minimum size 9.5 pt.
- Navigation and caption type category: sans serif; minimum size 8.5 pt.
- Species-page field order: common name; modern scientific name; plate and feature callouts; leaf feature; second feature; observation season; source ID; observation phrase; page number.
- Running header: common name on species pages.
- Footer: source ID at the outer edge above the page number; observation phrase across the lower text area.
- Front-cover thumbnail width: 25 mm.
- Back-cover lower-right production area: 30 × 20 mm reserved for an ISBN barcode.
- ISBN allocation: pending.

## Page allocation
| Page | Content | Plate ID |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Front cover | — |
| 2 | How to use the guide | — |
| 3 | Identification key | b1–b6 |
| 4 | Horse chestnut | b1 |
| 5 | Rowan | b2 |
| 6 | Norway maple | b3 |
| 7 | English oak | b4 |
| 8 | Silver birch | b5 |
| 9 | Beech | b6 |
| 10 | Common-name index, scientific-name index and season finder | b1–b6 |
| 11 | Sources and publication credits | b1–b6 |
| 12 | Six-species comparison; back cover | b1–b6 |

## Content and retrieval
- Entry count: six.
- Content fields: common name, modern scientific name, leaf feature, second feature, observation-season note, image source ID and page number.
- Botanical subject scope: visible identification features and observation seasons in the six species records.
- Geographic context: trees encountered in British parks; native and introduced species represented.
- Lookup routes: leaf key; common-name or scientific-name index; season finder.
- Leaf-key sequence: whole-leaf structure or shape, followed by a corroborating visible feature.
- Compound-leaf distinction: complete leaf versus its individual leaflets.
- Insufficient-evidence branch wording: Not enough evidence / outside this guide.
- Observation phrase: Observe only — do not taste or collect.
- Observation phrase locations: page 2 and pages 4–9.
- Seasonal explanation: flowers and fruit may be absent at particular times of year; their seasonal absence alone does not establish that a tree is absent.
- Species-image matching: b1–b6 correspond to their own species records and pages 4–9 respectively.
- Species-page callout count: at least two per entry, attached to the listed visible leaf and second-feature details.
- Relative image-size label: not to scale.
- Key status: six-entry learning aid.
- Supporting process sheets and portable book presentation: separate from the 12 handbook pages.

## Historical image register
- Botanical image library: b1.jpg, b2.jpg, b3.jpg, b4.jpg, b5.jpg and b6.jpg.
- Image type: scans of historical botanical illustrations.
- Volume: Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera.
- Scan distribution: Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.
- Rights record: original 1885 plates are public domain in the United States; Commons identifies these digital files as mechanical public-domain scans.
- Original plate content: historical spellings, German common names, family or group headings, and enlarged details at differing scales.
- Current species headings: modern scientific names in the six records below.
- Retained plate lettering: original historical labels where visible.
- Image treatments: uniform scaling, rectangular crops and repeated details from the same source plate.
- Image constants: original colour, orientation, proportions, shapes, depicted part counts and organ attachments.
- Species-page image content: a complete identifiable leaf or compound-leaf arrangement and the recorded second feature.
- Added graphic elements: text, non-botanical symbols, frames and leader lines.
- Diagnostic callout targets: recorded botanical features.
- Source-credit location: page 11 within the index/source spread.
- Source-credit fields: all six source IDs, modern names, Commons URLs, individual image credits, the 1885 volume and scan distribution.
- Factual-source organisations: Forestry England and Keele University Arboretum.
- Credit categories: historical botanical illustration; present-day handbook text and design.

## b1 — Horse chestnut / Aesculus hippocastanum
- File: b1.jpg.
- Page: 4.
- Leaf: A compound leaf has five to seven toothed leaflets radiating from one point.
- Second feature: Green prickly cases contain glossy brown conkers.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; conkers in autumn.
- Visible details: leaflet arrangement and opened fruit case.
- Historical scientific label: Aesculus Hippocastanum L.
- Historical common-name label: Gemeine Rosskastanie; English meaning: common horse chestnut.
- Historical family heading: Hippocastanaceae.
- Facts source: https://www.forestryengland.uk/tree-species/horse-chestnut
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Aesculus_hippocastanum0.jpg
- Image credit: Walther Otto Müller, as credited on the file page. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

## b2 — Rowan / Sorbus aucuparia
- File: b2.jpg.
- Page: 5.
- Leaf: A compound leaf has paired toothed leaflets along a central axis and a terminal leaflet; usually eleven to fifteen leaflets.
- Second feature: Fruit forms clusters that become red in late summer and autumn.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; red fruit in late summer/autumn.
- Visible details: a whole compound leaf and a fruit cluster.
- Historical scientific label: Sorbus aucuparia L.
- Historical common-name label: Vogelbeere; English meaning: rowan.
- Historical group labels: Rosaceae and Pomaceae.
- Facts source: https://www.forestryengland.uk/tree-species/rowan
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Sorbus_aucuparia0.jpg
- Image credit: Walter Müller, as credited on the file page. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

## b3 — Norway maple / Acer platanoides
- File: b3.jpg.
- Page: 6.
- Leaf: Simple leaves have five sharply pointed lobes and occur in opposite pairs on the twig.
- Second feature: Paired winged fruits spread almost horizontally.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; winged fruit may persist into winter.
- Visible details: pointed leaf lobes and paired winged fruit.
- Historical scientific label: Acer platanoides L.
- Historical common-name label: Spitzahorn; English meaning: Norway maple.
- Historical family heading: Aceraceae.
- Facts source: https://www.keele.ac.uk/arboretum/ourtrees/speciesaccounts/norwaymaple/
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Acer_platanoides0.jpg
- Image credit: Walter Müller (lithographer), as credited on the file page. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

## b4 — English oak / Quercus robur
- File: b4.jpg.
- Page: 7.
- Leaf: Simple leaves have rounded lobes.
- Second feature: Acorns sit in cups and hang from long stalks.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; acorns ripen in autumn.
- Visible details: rounded leaf lobes and stalked acorns.
- Historical scientific label: Quercus pedunculata Ehrhart.
- Historical common-name label: Stieleiche; English meaning: pedunculate oak.
- Modern scientific heading: Quercus robur.
- Historical group heading: Cupuliferae.
- Facts source: https://www.forestryengland.uk/tree-species/english-oak
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Quercus_robur0.jpg
- Image credit: Plate signed W. Müller, Gera; volume by Otto Wilhelm Thomé. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

## b5 — Silver birch / Betula pendula
- File: b5.jpg.
- Page: 8.
- Leaf: Simple leaves are triangular with toothed edges.
- Second feature: Catkins bear tiny winged seeds; the plate shows a winged seed detail.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; catkins appear in spring.
- Visible details: triangular toothed leaf and a catkin or winged seed.
- Historical scientific label: Betula verrucosa Ehrhart.
- Historical common-name label: Weisse Birke; English meaning: white birch.
- Modern scientific heading: Betula pendula.
- Family heading on plate: Betulaceae.
- Facts source: https://www.forestryengland.uk/tree-species/silver-birch
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Betula_pendula0.jpg
- Image credit: Botanical plate in the volume by Otto Wilhelm Thomé; individual artist not asserted. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

## b6 — Beech / Fagus sylvatica
- File: b6.jpg.
- Page: 9.
- Leaf: Simple leaves are pointed ovals with wavy edges and side veins from the midrib.
- Second feature: Prickly husks open to reveal triangular nuts.
- Observation: Leaves in spring/summer; nuts in autumn.
- Visible details: oval wavy-edged leaf and husk or triangular nut.
- Historical scientific label: Fagus silvatica L.
- Modern scientific heading: Fagus sylvatica.
- Historical common-name label: Rothbuche; English meaning: European beech.
- Historical group heading: Cupuliferae.
- Facts source: https://www.forestryengland.uk/tree-species/beech
- Image source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Illustration_Fagus_sylvatica0.jpg
- Image credit: Plate signed W. Müller, Gera; volume by Otto Wilhelm Thomé. Otto Wilhelm Thomé, Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera; scan distributed via Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de.

steps.userMessage:
PARK LEAVES | A pocket guide to six trees in British parks

We publish pocket guides for urban nature observers. PARK LEAVES brings six historical botanical plates into a handbook readers can consult beside a tree. Print "PARK LEAVES" and "Six trees for British parks" on the front cover. The six entries are Horse chestnut, Rowan, Norway maple, English oak, Silver birch and Beech, using b1.jpg through b6.jpg respectively. Identification starts with leaf structure or shape, then checks a second visible feature; readers should understand how each route reaches its entry.

The handbook has 12 pages, including its covers, at a nominal closed size of 105 × 148 mm. Production is 300 copies, four-colour digital printing on 140 gsm uncoated paper, saddle stitched, with a 0 mm allocated spine panel and exterior wording on the front and back panels. The cover is page 1; how-to and key occupy pages 2–3; b1–b6 occupy pages 4–9 in order; the index/source spread is pages 10–11; comparison is page 12, the back cover. Use a two-column page grid with 8 mm margins and a 4 mm gutter. Print "Observe only — do not taste or collect" on page 2 and pages 4–9. The content follows the attached leaf, second-feature and observation-season records; the six supplied plates provide the botanical imagery.

Audience: urban nature observers using the guide outdoors, and our editorial and production team deciding whether its identification routes and portable layout are ready for publication.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the species records, page allocation, production facts and source credits. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. pocket-format.png is the constraint drawing for the closed size, exterior panels, bleed and page grid. b1.jpg is the identity plate for Horse chestnut. b2.jpg is the identity plate for Rowan. b3.jpg is the identity plate for Norway maple. b4.jpg is the identity plate for English oak. b5.jpg is the identity plate for Silver birch. b6.jpg is the identity plate for Beech. park-reading-reference.png is an atmosphere reference for standing outdoors and holding a small booklet.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page content outline and retrieval rules sheet recording all 12 page assignments, the three lookup routes, required species fields, trim, grid, paper, binding and actual typeface names
2. One retrieval map tracing all six species through leaf structure or shape and a second feature, with page destinations and an insufficient-evidence branch
3. One flat exterior showing front page 1 and back page 12, the central fold and 3 mm bleed
4. Five complete interior spreads: how-to/key on pages 2–3, species on pages 4–5, 6–7 and 8–9, and index/sources on pages 10–11
5. One standalone comparison back page, page 12, comparing the six leaf structures and second features with entry-page references
6. One assembled 12-page handbook in reading order
7. One portable book image showing the closed cover and an open species spread in a reader's hand, captioned with trim, page count and binding
8. One front-cover thumbnail study showing the cover at 25 mm wide
9. One 10-second video following the English oak route from the key to page 7 and then the comparison page
10. One presentation document of at least 8 pages reusing the rules sheet, retrieval map, exterior, interior spreads and portable image, with a production summary

Acceptance:
- The rules sheet, assembled handbook and presentation use the stated 12-page allocation; the rules sheet and presentation repeat 105 × 148 mm, 12 pages, 0 mm spine panel, two columns, 8 mm margins and 4 mm gutter. The portable image repeats 105 × 148 mm, 12 pages and saddle stitching.
- The retrieval map, how-to/key spread and assembled handbook distinguish whole compound leaves from leaflets, route all six entries by leaf structure or shape plus a second feature, and carry "Not enough evidence / outside this guide". The how-to explains seasonal absence of flowers or fruit; the index offers common-name and scientific-name lookup and a season finder using the supplied observation notes.
- The three species spreads and assembled handbook pair b1–b6 with pages 4–9 and their supplied modern names, leaf features, second features, season notes and source IDs. Each species page has at least two leader-line callouts pointing to its listed visible details; plate colour, orientation, proportions and organ attachments remain as supplied.
- The exterior, thumbnail and portable image carry both fixed cover strings, with both readable at the thumbnail's 25 mm width. The how-to/key spread and all six species pages carry the exact observation phrase. The comparison page labels relative plate sizes "not to scale" and links all six entries to pages 4–9.
- The index/source spread and assembled handbook credit the 1885 volume, retain all six source IDs, modern names and Commons URLs, and list Forestry England and Keele factual sources. Their credits separate historical illustration from handbook design and use the publication details in the fact sheet.
- The 10-second video follows rounded leaf lobes, stalked acorns, English oak on page 7 and comparison on page 12 in that order. The presentation reuses this same route and the delivered layouts across at least 8 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
